items.evidence: product-rename.spec.ts:140-144 reloads the page, then asserts the name input value and header title are 'E2E Zip Hoodie'. Both would fail if the mutation never ran.
AC1 is covered at spec lines 135 and 137 (header title and browser title after save). AC2 is covered at lines 142-143 (name field and header title after reload).
No existing page object covers the product page or global search. ProductPage and SearchPage duplicate nothing in e2e/pages, e2e/lib or e2e/scenarios, and PRODUCTS/ORDERS_SCENARIO are reused.
No waitForTimeout, sleeps or polling loops.
Imports test/expect from ../../fixtures/test.ts, has no parallel() tag, and writes nothing to the cache or dumps.
Locators use data-test-id or role and name (page-header, button-bar-confirm, the Name textbox, the Products radio), and the title is scoped to the header. No CSS, XPath or positional selectors.
Data comes from ORDERS_SCENARIO. The spec only navigates to the existing product and creates nothing.
Uses PRODUCTS.hoodie.name from the scenario. The product is reached by search, not a hard-coded id.
Uses the default admin session from the fixture. There is no UI login and no credentials.
typecheck.txt reports exit 0, and the spec is in e2e/tests/products/.
All locators and multi-step actions live on ProductPage/SearchPage. The spec only calls methods and asserts on page-object locators.
Both classes use readonly fields initialised from this.page and constructor(readonly page: Page) {}.
The spec has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments (lines 113 and 118).
One test with three named test.step stages.
The title 'Staff renames a product #e2e' describes the behaviour and carries the tag.
A doc comment at spec lines 101-107 explains what is covered and why search is not re-checked.
All assertions are web-first (toHaveValue, toBeVisible, toHaveTitle, toBeDisabled).
Old name and scenario come from the scenario's constants. The new name is a ticket value the scenario does not have, held in one constant.
No cleanup steps and no unique or random names.
No explicit timeouts, retries or networkidle. Waits target named UI or URL states.
Relative imports keep .ts. Page objects import expect from @playwright/test, as draftOrderPage.ts and homePage.ts already do, and the spec uses the fixture.
No any, no casts and no gql calls.
Comments explain reasons: why save() waits on the button, why search is used, and why the header keeps the old name.
